Results.ReviewText:
The classic, all-purpose grill, and it also serves as a smoker. 
I recently gave away my old smoker, as it was too large for my purposes, and took up too much space in my garage. In my search for a new grill/smoker, I came to realize that the Weber Kettle grill was absolutely perfect for my needs. 
To grill, I stack the charcoal in the middle of the lower grate, and things go per the usual plan. 
To smoke, I line the charcoal around the elipse of one side, along with the wood chips, and I place the meat on the top grill surface on the other elipse. 
Perfection every time!!
Results.Title: Simply the best grill!

My one complaint is that they changed the direction of the top handle 90 degrees, so to hang the lid on the kettle is difficult, or requires two hands, definitely not an improvement.  Other than that, it's great to have, especially, chicken over charcoal.  It just doesn't come out the same on a smoker or grill.

Results.ReviewText: Weber over the years has cheapened their grills. The metal is a thinner gauge steel making it harder to hold heat and keep temps. The lid needs a gasket to seal. A sloppy fitting lid allows air in and this will also affect your temps. They switched the venting to a vent/ash clean out. This was the worse idea as, one it doesn’t seal the air intakes that well again  making it difficult to hold temps. Two it clogs with grease and will get hard to move and then the wings bend. They should have stuck to the original Weber kettle. Heavy gauge steel,  disk dampers which are/were the best. I own the old and have owned several of the old style and they just perform with competition worthy BBQ. I’ll continue to look for old ones at rummage sales . As far as the new onesI ,throw them in the trash. Wake up Weber make the old ones again.
Results.Title: Bring back the old Weber Kettle

Results.ReviewText: The grill works just fine and the food is always delicious. Its my first Weber, ever, and I use it every week. However this specific grill is quite limited in three major ways. 1) the plate that serves as an ash catcher is horrible. If you get some wind or a breeze that ash is getting tossed into the grass/surrounding area. 2) No thermometer to gauge the temperature, and 3) I wish my grill had some built on hooks to hold tongs, spatula, etc. A big pain in the butt to keep all that stuff elsewhere nearby. All in all the lesson learned is NOT to get cheap with the grill and trying to save some money. For those looking to get their first ever Weber, I highly suggest getting one with the pan as the ash catcher and a thermometer. Remember: if you're lookin' you aint cookin'
Results.Title: Don't cut corners with money!

Results.ReviewText: After four years, my new Weber Kettle grill is rusting out where the pop welds hold up the charcoal grate. Each of the  pop welds are rusting out in the same manner. My weber is never exposed to the elements, and I use a heavy duty cover. All other areas of the grill are fine. No rust present. I can only assume the issue is a factory defect. I purchased a new weber because I had my old one for 25 years. When I moved, I treated myself to a new grill. However, the new grill is rusting which has never happened to me before with a Weber. They clearly are not the same quality and not worth the price. I should have kept my old  one.
